name: FL Studio
note: Every keyboard row of Image-Line's "Keyboard & Mouse Shortcuts" page of the FL Studio online manual. The context is the manual's own table heading (File Operations, Pattern Selector, Channel Rack & Step Sequencer, Record / Playback / Transport, Window Navigation, Mixer, Playlist, Piano roll, Browser, Miscellaneous Commands); the two rows the page lists under "Global Shortcuts" carry no context. The page documents Windows chords and a "Windows vs Mac Equivalent keys" table (Ctrl = Cmd, Alt = Opt, Backspace = delete, Delete = fn+delete, Insert = fn+return, Windows key = Cmd); the mac chords here are that mapping applied, and mac is omitted for the rows that use Delete or Insert because fn+delete and fn+return are not expressible in this grammar. Where the manual writes both forms itself ("Ctrl/Cmd+X", "Ctrl+Enter/Cmd+Return") its own spelling is used. Rows whose key is a range or a pair ("Alt/Opt+0,1..9", "Ctrl/Cmd+1..9,0", "Shift + 1 to 3", "Alt/Opt+Left-Arrow/Right-Arrow", "PgUp/PgDown", "Alt/Opt+Arrow keys") are split into one action per key with the key appended to the name in parentheses. Left out: every mouse row (clicks, double-clicks, mouse-wheel, middle-click, pan/drag), the rows that need a side-specific modifier (Left-Shift, Right-Alt, Right-Shift), the numpad rows (the Pattern Selector table is headed "(Numpad)", plus Fast forward / Next bar / Previous bar and "Alt/Opt+Number-Pad 2-6"), and "Alt/Opt+/*" (Jump to Next/Previous song marker), which are numpad keys the grammar cannot name. Note from the manual: the single-key shortcuts only work when "Typing keyboard to piano" (Ctrl/Cmd+T) is off.
